transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah… I guess I came in because at work I’ve had to be in front of people more, like meetings and events and photos and all that, and I keep noticing this one part of my face that looks uneven to me. 

It’s mostly in pictures—like I’ll zoom in and stare at it, and then I can’t stop thinking about it, even though people say they barely notice anything. I know that sounds kind of… maybe not like a big reason to be here, but it’s been really bothering me.
Is it always the same part of your face that looks uneven to you?

Yeah, it’s pretty much the same spot. I mean, it’s this uneven-looking part of my face that I keep seeing in photos, especially now that I’m in front of people more at work. Like at events, someone will take a group picture and everyone else is just looking at the whole photo, and I’m there zooming in on that one area.

And people tell me they barely see it, but I don’t know… once I notice it, I can’t really unsee it.
Is this concern about your face affecting your daily activities or relationships outside of work?

Yeah… I mean, outside of work it’s not like I’m fighting with people over it or anything, but it kind of spills into everything. Like, I’ll be trying to get ready for something and then I end up messing with my hair or angles or whatever for way too long.

At work it’s definitely caused problems too—like I actually missed part of a planning deadline because I spent so much time looking at how I came across in the event materials. And now even normal stuff, like vendor calls or prepping for meetings, takes longer than it should because I get stuck thinking about it or trying to make sure I won’t look weird.
Do you ever find yourself performing specific rituals or behaviors in an attempt to temporarily alleviate your concerns about your face?

Yeah… I do. I don’t know if I’d call them rituals, but before I send event pictures or before I’m about to join a vendor meeting, I’ll check my face in my phone camera a bunch of times. Like, I’ll retake photos, tilt my head a certain way, try to find the “right” angle.

And sometimes I’ll ask a coworker, like, “Do I look weird?” which is embarrassing because they’re usually just trying to get the event materials done. But then I get stuck on it, and suddenly I’ve spent all this time checking instead of actually planning, and I end up falling behind on stuff.
Do you feel less anxious when you're able to check your face in the camera or find the right angle?

Yeah… kind of. Like, for a minute I feel better if I can get the angle right or if the phone camera looks okay. But then it doesn’t really last, because I’ll check again before sending pictures or before a vendor meeting.

It’s annoying because I’ll start out just trying to do something quick, like review event photos, and then I’m retaking them or tilting my head and trying to make sure I don’t look weird. Sometimes I’ll even ask a coworker, which I hate doing because they’re busy too. And then suddenly I’ve wasted all this time and I’m behind on planning stuff.
Are you trying to fix something that you think is wrong with your face, or are you trying to avoid being seen as ugly or unattractive by others?

I think it’s more… I’m trying not to have people see it and think I look bad. Like, I don’t know if I can “fix” it exactly, but I keep focusing on this one part of my face that looks uneven to me in photos.

That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. Since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, like for events and pictures and stuff, I just can’t stop staring at it. Other people say they barely notice anything, but I’ll still zoom in or look at the photo over and over, and then I start thinking everyone else is going to see it too.
Is your main concern that this one part of your face is uneven, or is it more that you don't want to look unattractive in general?

It’s mostly that one part, I think… the uneven-looking part. Like, I know everyone wants to look decent in photos, especially with work stuff, but this feels more specific than that.

Ever since I’ve had to be more in front of people at events and in pictures, I just keep staring at that area of my face. I’ll see it in a photo and then I can’t unsee it, even if someone else says they barely notice anything. Then I start wondering if everyone else is noticing it too, and I get kind of stuck on it.
Is your concern about this uneven part of your face related to a fear that you're unattractive overall, or is it really just about fixing this one specific area?

It’s… I think it’s mostly that one area, not like my whole face is ugly or something. Or, I don’t know, it turns into that sometimes because if that part looks off in a picture then I feel like the whole photo is ruined.

But the thing I keep coming back to is that uneven-looking part. That’s why I came in, really. Since I’ve had to be in front of people more at work—events, photos, all that—I can’t stop staring at it in pictures, even when people say they barely see anything. Then I’m like, okay, but I see it, so maybe everyone else does too.
Do you think you would still be concerned about this uneven part of your face if you were completely alone and didn't have to interact with anyone?

I mean… if I were completely alone, maybe it wouldn’t be as loud in my head? I’m not sure. It really got bad because of work, because I’ve had to be in front of people more, like at events and in photos and those group pictures everyone posts afterward.

And then I see that one uneven-looking part of my face, and I just start staring at it. Like I’ll zoom in, or compare it to another picture, even if people tell me they barely see anything. So… I think being around people and knowing they might see the photos makes it worse. But I still notice it myself once I see it.
Would your concern about the uneven part of your face go away if you were certain that no one else could see it?

I don’t know if it would totally go away. I mean, I think it got really bad because of being more visible at work—events, photos, people posting pictures afterward, that kind of thing. Like I came in because I can’t stop staring at this one uneven-looking part of my face in photos, even when other people say they barely see anything.

If I were absolutely sure no one else could see it, maybe I’d feel less panicky about it. But I’d still see it, if that makes sense. Like once I notice it in a picture, I kind of lock onto it. And then I start thinking about it even if the original reason was other people seeing it.
Do you think your concern about the uneven part of your face would decrease if you were certain that everyone who saw you or your pictures thought you looked fine?

Maybe… somewhat? If everyone honestly thought I looked fine, I think that would take off some pressure, because a lot of it started when I had to be more in front of people at work, like events and photos and all that.

But I don’t know if it would just disappear, because I’m still the one staring at the picture. Like even when people say they barely see anything, I keep going back to that one uneven part of my face. And then I start thinking, okay, maybe they’re just being nice, or maybe it’s more obvious in certain lighting—sorry, I know that’s not exactly what you asked. But yeah, it might decrease, but I’d probably still notice it.
Do you think you would be concerned about the uneven part of your face if it was only visible to you, and not to anyone else?

Yeah… I think I would, at least some. Like, I know that sounds kind of weird if no one else could see it, but I’m still the one looking at the photos, you know?

It really started getting bad because of work, though—like since I’ve had to be in front of people more at events, and then there are pictures afterward, and sometimes coworkers post them and I’ll be like, oh no, that angle. And then I end up staring at that one uneven-looking part of my face even if everyone says they barely notice anything.

So if it was only visible to me, maybe I wouldn’t be as embarrassed or worried about other people noticing, but I think I’d still get stuck on it once I saw it.
Is your concern about the uneven part of your face more about the way it looks to you or about what others might think of you when they see it?

I think it’s kind of both, but… it starts with how it looks to me, I guess. Like I’ll see a photo and immediately my eyes go to that uneven part of my face, and then I can’t really unsee it.

But the reason it’s gotten so bad is probably because of work, being in front of people more—events, pictures, people posting them afterward. I’ll be planning something and then afterward I’m not even thinking about the event, I’m looking at the pictures like, “Oh my god, is that what my face looked like?” Even when everyone says they barely notice anything, I still keep staring at it. So it’s my own view of it, but then I worry other people are seeing what I’m seeing too.
Is your concern about the uneven part of your face driven more by the fact that you think it's flawed or by the fear that others will judge you because of it?

I think… more because I think it’s flawed, honestly. Like the judging part makes it worse, especially at work when I’m in front of people more, but it starts with me seeing it.

That’s kind of why I came in, because in photos I’ll just lock onto this one uneven-looking part of my face and I can’t stop staring at it. And then someone will say, “I barely see what you mean,” but I’m already zooming in or thinking about the lighting or the angle. Sorry, I’m going off a little. But yeah, it’s the flaw I think I see first, and then I worry other people will notice it too.
Is your concern about the uneven part of your face something you think is inherently wrong with your appearance, or is it more about how you believe others might perceive you because of it?

I think it’s more like… I feel like it’s actually wrong with my face, if that makes sense. Like it starts with me seeing the uneven part and feeling like, no, that looks bad, that doesn’t look right.

But then I get pulled into what other people might think too, especially because of work. Since I’ve had to be more in front of people at events and stuff, there are always photos afterward, and I’ll see one and just get stuck staring at that one part of my face. Even if someone says they barely notice anything, I’m like, how do you not see it? And then I’m thinking about whether everyone else at the event noticed it too.

Sorry, I know I kind of went around the question. I guess the short answer is it feels wrong to me first, and then I worry other people are seeing it the same way.
Do you think you would still try to fix or hide the uneven part of your face if you were completely alone and had no fear of others seeing it?

Yeah… I think I probably would, honestly. Like even if no one else was going to see me, I still notice it. It’s not only about people judging me.

I mean, the whole reason I came in is because since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, it’s gotten way worse—like events, photos afterward, all of that. But when I look at the pictures, I’m the one who can’t stop staring at that uneven-looking part of my face. Even when everyone else says they barely see anything, I still see it right away.

So… yeah, I think I’d still want to fix it or hide it, even alone. Maybe not as intensely without the work stuff and people seeing photos, but it would still bother me.
Is your desire to fix the uneven part of your face driven by wanting to correct what you see as a flaw or by wanting to avoid being judged by others?

I think it’s more wanting to correct it, like… I look at photos and that uneven part just jumps out at me, and I can’t stop staring at it.

But then, I mean, because my job has me in front of people more now—events, photos, all that—it also turns into worrying what people think. Like I’ll be looking through event pictures and everyone else is talking about the room setup or the guests, and I’m just stuck on my face. Even if someone says they barely see anything, I still see it. So I guess it starts as wanting to fix the flaw I see, and then the judgment part piles on after.
Is your desire to fix the uneven part of your face driven by the fact that you think it's inherently unattractive or because you fear others will notice and judge you?

I think it’s… more that I see it as unattractive first. Like, I’ll see a photo from an event and everyone else is focused on normal stuff, like how the setup looked or whether the lighting was good, and I’m just staring at that one uneven part of my face.

And I know people tell me they barely notice it, but I don’t know, I notice it immediately. Since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, it’s made it harder to ignore, because there are more pictures and more chances to see it. So yes, I do worry people will judge it, but it starts with me feeling like it just looks wrong.
Is your desire to fix the uneven part of your face something you would still have if you knew for certain that no one else would ever see your face or judge your appearance?

Yeah… I think I would. I mean, it got a lot worse because of work, because I’m more in front of people now and there are all these event photos afterward, and then I end up zooming in or just staring at that one uneven-looking part of my face.

Like, even when other people are saying they barely see anything, I still see it right away. So if no one else could ever see me, I guess the pressure would be less, but I don’t think it would just disappear. I’d still be bothered by it because I’m the one looking at it.
